text:
sam: Heads up — seeing a long tail in generation latency for eu-west since 08:12 UTC. Spike looks tied to 3 tenants blasting short-context streams. Shared-gpu pool (shared-pool-2) is saturated. Anyone oncall?
jules: Oncall — looking. can you paste the allocation ids and which AZ?
sam: allocs: t-33a, t-19b, t-77c. All in eu-west-1a. 90% of active queues from those tenants. 95th latency jumped from ~120ms -> ~900ms. NVLink queue depth high per telemetry.
maria: ack. can you confirm they're on shared-pool-2 (eu-west-1a) and not already in a burst reserve?
sam: confirmed shared-pool-2, not in reserved lanes. egress counters also spike (outbound bytes per second high).
kevin: quick mitigation option: soft-handoff to burst/reserved lane. we have nodeSelector label dedicated=burst for short-term. can do graceful move to avoid slab OOMs.
jules: prefer graceful. kevin — run the drain with --grace 60 so other slices don't get preempted hard. also watch KV cache pressure.
kevin: running handoff now: /usr/local/bin/handoff.sh --tenants t-33a,t-19b,t-77c --to burst-pool-euwest --grace 60 :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ops-bot: deploy-bot: handoff job queued id=hf-20231114-09 ; ETA ~45s
ops-bot: Telemetry note: eviction rate in shared-pool-2 = 0.8% over last 10m (baseline 0.1%).
maria: additionally, let's throttle per-tenant egress to reduce NVLink pressure. set temporary cap to 100Mbps per tenant.
sam: +1 to throttle. kevin can you apply egress tc?
kevin: applied egress shaping for t-33a,t-19b,t-77c. command used:
```
# tc htb snippet (applied via infra-run)
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:10 htb rate 100mbit ceil 100mbit
# iptables match by tenant-ip and mark to class 1:10
```
jules: Good. On routing side we should consider a short-term auto-fallback rule: if tenant.burst > 80% for 3m -> route to reserved-mini-pool and notify ops. Can someone add a transient rule in the router?
maria: I'll open a quick PR for the router-policy and add a feature flag. For now, kevin can we do a local rule?
kevin: added temp router rule: if tenant(t-33a|t-19b|t-77c) sustained >0.8 for 180s -> pool=reserved-mini, priority=low, notify=ops. Pushed and toggled live under ff:tenant-burst-fallback.
sam: latency trending down. 95th now ~220ms (was 900ms). keep monitoring for KV cache misses.
ops-bot: Monitoring update: 95th latency = 240ms; eviction events during handoff = 2; handoff job hf-20231114-09 status=SUCCESS.
kevin: quick FYI on cost — moving to burst pool increases GPU-hours cost for EUWest by an estimated ~12% if sustained over next 12h. we should notify billing owners.
maria: noted. I'll message tenant owners and add billing note. also add a runbook entry under infra/runbooks/tenant-burst-handoff.
jules: action items: 1) add auto-fallback rule to router RFC (maria) 2) create incident tracker card if this recurs (sam) 3) add cost alert for burst pool usage (kevin).
sam: I'll ping tenant teams and keep this thread updated. thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin: closing loop — will monitor NVLink and egress for next 30m. ping here if anything spikes.
ops-bot: closing telemetry snapshot attached to incident id=inc-20231114-eu-burst (summary: handoff success, 95th reduced, cost spike potential).
